bc_big_rock.blurb: A single large boulder standing on the ocean side of the old Island Highway, just south of Campbell River on Vancouver Island. It holds 16 problems, from VB-level up to about V6, with most landing between V2 and V5, and faces on the south, east and north sides. Problems are numbered around the block starting at the left of the south face. Because the boulder sits at the water's edge, the tide matters: in winter it can cover the base, which may rule out some sit starts on the east and north sides. Expect a roadside, quick-stop session rather than a destination day, and a boulder that often carries graffiti.

bc_l_mantel_madness.blurb: A sector of the Grand Wall Boulders, the cool, mossy forest of blocks beneath the Stawamus Chief near Squamish. This sector has 16 problems, a few easy ones to start, then mostly V3 through V8, with one far harder outlier at the top end. It suits strong boulderers more than beginners, and the shaded setting makes it a good choice on warm summer days. Walk in from the Chief's main lot toward the campground, then branch into the forest; most sectors in this boulder field are a 5 to 10 minute stroll from the car.
bc_l_mantel_madness.approach: From the Chief's main lot, follow the wide gravel path toward the campground; within a few minutes forest trails branch left to the boulders. Most sectors are a 5 to 10 minute walk.

bc_ronin_s_corner.blurb: A small crag in the Smoke Bluffs, the municipal park of short granite cliffs on the edge of Squamish. It has 16 climbs, mostly trad with a handful of sport lines, protected by bolts, gear or a mix of both. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.11, with the bulk sitting around 5.10, so it is better for climbers with some leading experience than for rank beginners, though a few gentler lines exist. Routes are single pitch and the walk from the parking lot is short, making it an easy half-day stop within the wider bluffs.

bc_pixie_corner.blurb: A tight group of climbs, cracks for the most part, tucked into the forest uphill of Neat and Cool in Squamish's Smoke Bluffs. Of its 16 climbs, 14 are trad and two are sport. Difficulty is wide, from moderate 5.7 cracks through a good number of 5.11 lines to a few 5.12 pitches, with a double-dihedral corner as the centrepiece. The easier cracks can be walked off or topped out to set an anchor, which makes them popular for first leads and top-rope laps. Routes are one pitch and short, so it works as a quick stop or a warm-up for trad-minded parties.

bc_supratidal_zawn_copper_cove_wall.blurb: A sea-level wall at Copper Cove, a small waterfront crag in West Vancouver on Howe Sound, a short drive from the Horseshoe Bay ferry. It holds 16 climbs, mainly sport with a good number of trad lines and one aid pitch. Grades start near 5.8 and run to 5.12, with the largest group around 5.10; the sport lines run roughly 20 m. The base is only comfortably reached when the tide is low, so plan the day around the tide tables. Expect a scenic, ocean-edge outing rather than a quiet backcountry crag.
